summary.headline: UGRO Q1 FY27: total AUM INR 15,013 crore and disbursements INR 2,551 crore (+59% YoY); opex cut to ~INR 119 crore from INR 217 crore in Q4.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 reflected the completed shift toward Emerging Market LAP and Embedded Merchant Finance (GROx), which together reached 46% of AUM versus 32% in Dec '25. Interest income fell 13% QoQ to INR 363 crore as co-lending and direct assignment income dropped to INR 75 crore from INR 155 crore, though it grew 19% YoY. Quarterly opex fell 42% QoQ to ~INR 119 crore, and reported PAT was lifted by a one-time deferred tax reversal from the move to the new tax regime (pre-tax ROA 2.6% vs reported 2.8%). Management guided AUM flat for FY27 with on-balance-sheet assets growing, and said growth can be funded without incremental equity through FY29. Q&A focused on runoff, GNPA trajectory, the Profectus merger and the weak share price.

financial_highlights.change: Down from INR 155 crore in Q4 FY26; ~14% of total income vs 24% in Q4
Cost of borrowing down 41 bps YoY; 7th consecutive quarterly improvement
Down from INR 217 crore in Q4 FY26 (-42% QoQ); -2% YoY
Gap driven by one-time deferred tax reversal

segments.name: Emerging Market LAP
segments.commentary: AUM rose to INR 3,896 crore from INR 3,581 crore in March (~9% QoQ); disbursed INR 592 crore in Q1. Yield ~18.5%, GNPA ~2.1% (1.2% in March). 317 branches across 13 states; blended productivity INR 62 lakh per branch per month vs ~INR 48 lakh in FY26.

segments.name: Embedded Merchant Finance (GROx)
segments.commentary: AUM rose to INR 3,003 crore from INR 2,280 crore in March (~32% QoQ); disbursed INR 1,853 crore in Q1, >60,000 loans a month, ~3.4 lakh active customers. Yield ~26%, GNPA 2.1% (1.7% in March).

segments.name: Prime Intermediate (defocused, DSA-led)
segments.commentary: Run-off continuing off-balance sheet; carries 3.1% GNPA. Management says run-off is ~25% vs 20% planned. The DSA foreclosure cost was recognised upfront this quarter, which pressured interest income.

guidance_outlook: Total AUM expected flat in FY27, with on-balance-sheet assets growing modestly.
Emerging Market and GROx targeted at ~25% CAGR to FY29; defocused Prime book to run down ~20% (actual run-off ~25%). Management indicated ~15% growth overall.
FY27 opex guidance ~INR 490 crore; management says opex now flat from Q1 run-rate, excluding inflation.
Co-lending and DA share of income to fall to ~4% over the next 11-12 quarters; income expected to stay in the current quarter's range for the transition year.
Pre-tax ROA path to 3-3.5%; the adjusted base is ~2.1% per management.
EM LAP credit cost guidance of 1.5-2% reiterated; peak EM LAP delinquency expected at 3-3.5% (3.5-4% cited as projected peak) and Embedded Finance not beyond 3%.

Profectus merger filed with NCLT; completion expected by Q3 FY27 if fortunate, and before Q4 FY27 at the latest. Post-merger net worth may fall (non-cash goodwill set-off), with no capital adequacy impact.
No incremental equity needed through FY29. Dividend to be reviewed around Q3/Q4 FY27; most likely capital is retained for growth.
capex_capacity: EM branch network at 317 branches; branch build-out complete, so focus shifted to productivity. Mature (>12 months) branches number 96 (from 81 in March) and produce ~INR 81 lakh per month vs target INR 80-85 lakh.
~145 branches are under 6 months old; target is INR 75-80 lakh monthly disbursement once they cross 12 months.
Net worth INR 2,976 crore; standalone CRAR 21%, expected ~23-24% on a merged basis.
Liquidity of INR 1,864 crore; incremental long-term borrowing at ~9.8%, below the average cost of liabilities.
demand_pricing: Combined EM and GROx share of AUM 46% (from 32% in Dec '25), targeted at 85% by FY29.
GROx partners: onboarding other lenders, with SIDBI as a co-lending partner, and more banks and NBFCs coming. Average EM LAP ticket size INR 17 lakh (range INR 7.5-50 lakh).
Competitive pressure: large lenders are taking over the Prime run-off book, which is accelerating run-off. Management says it may reduce rates to retain customers.
July 2026 monthly disbursement crossed INR 1,000 crore for the first time.

qa_highlights.question: Amit Mehendale asked for closing AUM expectations for FY27 and FY28, and the expected year-end ROE.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects AUM flat in FY27 with on-balance-sheet assets growing modestly, since runoff is mainly off-balance-sheet Prime book. No FY28 point guidance; FY29 framework is EM LAP and GROx at ~25% CAGR and Prime run-off at 20% (actual ~25%), implying ~15% overall growth.

qa_highlights.question: Neel Advani asked how much of the sequential interest income decline was old-book reversal versus disbursement timing, and when interest income would recover to Q4 levels.
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split the decline on the call and promised to revert. It said Q1 is the base, interest income should rise sequentially as on-book assets grow, opex stays flat from Q1 run-rate, and co-lending/DA income stays in the current range during the transition year.

qa_highlights.question: Neel Advani asked whether the ROA path of 3-3.5% is on reported or normalised basis, given the tax reversal.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA adjusted for the one-time tax reversal is about 2.1%, and the 3-3.5% trajectory is built off that base.

qa_highlights.question: Neel Advani asked whether the EM LAP GNPA rise (1.2% to 2.1%) and Embedded GNPA rise (1.7% to 2.1%) were running ahead of the model, and whether the 1.5-2% EM LAP credit cost guidance holds.
qa_highlights.answer: Anuj Pandey said peak EM LAP delinquency is projected at 3.5-4% once average months on book pass 18 (currently ~15), settling at 3-3.5%; Embedded Finance peak should not exceed 3%. Shachindra Nath reiterated the 1.5-2% EM LAP credit cost guidance and said GNPA may rise to 3.5% without credit cost rising proportionately.

qa_highlights.question: Neel Advani asked about the Profectus merger timeline and post-merger capital adequacy.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said completion is targeted by end-Q3 FY27 if fortunate, and before Q4 FY27 at the latest. CFO said standalone CRAR is 21% and merged-basis CRAR should be about 23-24%, not the 27-28% suggested.

qa_highlights.question: Rishi asked whether the Prime/DSA book could be sold in one block, as Profectus was acquired.
qa_highlights.answer: Anuj Pandey said no: portfolio sales need 6 months' vintage, collection infrastructure would become uneconomic, negative carry on excess cash, and a large income reversal on the off-balance-sheet component. Run-off will remain the standard explanation for another 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Rishi asked about dividends and buybacks, given cash on hand and ~INR 300 crore expected FY27 profit.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buybacks are not possible for NBFCs under Companies Act leverage limits (2x). Dividend policy would need an RBI-compliant change and shareholder approval; FY27 profit includes assignment income, and the final call comes in Q3/Q4 FY27, with capital most likely retained for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Kamal asked about the main execution risks beyond the next two quarters, including the sub-2% GNPA thesis, opex and profitability.
qa_highlights.answer: Shachindra Nath pointed to Slide 21 productivity inflection and said the 145 branches under 6 months must reach INR 75-80 lakh monthly disbursement after 12 months. Other risks: larger-ticket, longer-tenure Embedded loans raising credit risk, and faster Prime runoff from competitors reducing income.

risks_watch: Credit: EM LAP delinquency peak of 3-3.5% (3.5-4% cited) and Embedded Finance cap of 3%; watch whether GNPA on AUM (2.6%) and segment GNPA rise beyond guidance.

Income transition: co-lending/DA income is ~14% of total income and is expected to fall to ~4% over 11-12 quarters; interest income reversals from faster Prime runoff (~25% vs 20% planned) could pressure P&L.

Merger execution: Profectus scheme filed with NCLT; completion timing (Q3 to pre-Q4 FY27) and post-merger net worth reduction from goodwill set-off, with CRAR moving from 21% standalone to ~23-24% merged.

Growth funding without equity: AUM guided flat for FY27; management says ~15% growth through FY29. Monitor on-balance-sheet asset growth and branch productivity (96 mature branches, 145 branches under 6 months).

Governance and shareholder sentiment: a special resolution on enabling variable pay was voted down by some institutions on proxy advice; share price near 0.5x book, with sponsor exits cited as an overhang.
Cost of borrowing (10.14%) and the mix of long-term funding; management did not include further borrowing-cost declines in its projections.
key_quotes: The combined contribution of Emerging Market and Embedded Merchant Finance increased from 32% of total asset under management in December '25 to 46% in June '26.
Basis this strategy, we are confident that UGRO can achieve its planned growth without incremental equity through FY29.

Consequently, our reported net worth may reduce. This would be a non-cash accounting adjustment and would not impact capital adequacy as these amounts are already deducted while computing the regulatory capital.
Most likely, it looks like that the growth momentum which we are getting, we would need to preserve more capital for augmenting our growth versus taking out the cash.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic transition, operating momentum and funding, but defensive on the share price, runoff explanations and asset-quality trajectory. Management avoided giving FY28 numbers and deferred the interest-income bifurcation and dividend decisions to later quarters.

growth.why: Management guides total AUM flat for FY27 with on-balance-sheet assets growing modestly, and ~25% EM/GROx CAGR to FY29 (~15% overall); backing is partial, relying on branch productivity, GROx share gains and cost cuts (opex ~INR 490 crore FY27) rather than specific new capacity or orders.
